label: rare: early original-phase token after o (esp. after "o o"); also some copy-phase f/t
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.026% of steps). The strongest single cue is that the previous input is o during the original phase, mostly at t=2-3 (about 40% of mass), and the strongest activations come after the bigram "o o" (e.g. s t o o [2]). But prev_tok==o fires on fewer than 1% of matching steps. About 45% of mass is in the copy phase, mostly on f/t inputs in sequences that start with or contain p (p f y p <DEL> p [f]), and those conjunctions also have very low precision. Never fires at t=0-1. The best predicate ("o o" then the current token) reaches only F1 of about 0.12. No coherent token-level description was found.
